Research · merging your own PR when a ruleset lets you bypass review
How Nod gates merge today
Nod already has Admin merge: desktop review bar (M) and the phone More sheet. It runs
gh pr merge --admin (shared/pr-actions.ts, adminMergeArgs).
It shows only on your own PR (or one whose head commit you pushed), and only when
canAdminMerge() is true: viewerCanMergeAsAdmin, or repo permission ADMIN
(server/github-map.ts).
The server re-checks author, permission, open, not draft and check rollup SUCCESS
before it runs gh (adminMerge in server/github-provider.ts).
OWN_PR_HINT, "Your PR: GitHub only allows comments", shows whenever ownPr, whatever
the merge options (DetailPane ReviewBar, ReviewPane, phone body line).
Does viewerCanMergeAsAdmin cover this case? No
GraphQL docs: "Indicates whether the viewer can bypass branch protections and merge
the pull request immediately." It names branch protections, not rulesets.
Nod's own comment says the field ignores ruleset bypass lists, and this case agrees:
a team bypass actor without ADMIN saw only Comment.
Whether GitHub ever sets it for ruleset bypass actors: unverified. Treat it as not
covering team bypass, so a ruleset check is needed.
How the merge is sent
GraphQL mergePullRequest has no admin flag. gh --admin skips the merge queue and
auto-merge and calls mergePullRequest directly. GitHub applies the bypass on its side
when the viewer is a bypass actor (from gh source, unverified this session).
So the send path exists: reuse adminMerge and gh pr merge --admin. Only the gate is
new.
Method today comes from the title rule (squash + delete branch, merge for release
titles). For the repo's allowed method, add squashMergeAllowed, mergeCommitAllowed,
rebaseMergeAllowed and deleteBranchOnMerge to the detail query. No extra call.
Telling "only review required" apart
Show when all hold: own PR, OPEN, not draft, mergeable MERGEABLE, mergeStateStatus
BLOCKED, check rollup SUCCESS, reviewDecision REVIEW_REQUIRED, zero unresolved
threads (reviewThreads isResolved, already fetched).
Hide on CHANGES_REQUESTED, BEHIND, DIRTY, failing or pending checks, or any
unresolved thread.
BLOCKED can also hide rules Nod cannot see (signed commits, deployments). GitHub
refuses those and Nod shows its text.
reviewThreads reads the last 50. A PR with more threads should hide the action.
REST ruleset calls, cost and caching
Only when the gate passes: GET /repos/{o}/{r}/rules/branches/{base} (1 call) lists
rules with ruleset_id.
Keep pull_request rules with required_approving_review_count of 1 or more. The org
threads ruleset (0 approvals) drops out.
Then GET /repos/{o}/{r}/rulesets/{id} per kept id, usually 1. current_user_can_bypass
always or pull_requests_only shows the action; never hides it.
Uses the REST core budget (5,000 an hour), not GraphQL points. Send If-None-Match; a
304 is free.
Cache per repo and base for 1 hour in repo-meta, like teams. Worst case about 2 calls
per repo per hour. A 403 or 404 counts as no bypass.
Whether the repo endpoint returns org-level rulesets for a non-admin: unverified.
